title: gpg: sign the challenge with gpg-agent
description:
hire-attestors/src/gpg.rs enumerates keys by parsing 'gpg --with-colons' (:139-147) and applies the enrolment rule recorded in the gpg-key-validity-policy memory, but inherits the default prove() and so produces no evidence.

Closest sibling to ssh.rs, which is the model: connect to the agent, have it sign the daemon's challenge, verify the signature against both the challenge and the key the candidate names. gpg-agent speaks Assuan over its socket; the key never leaves the agent.

Assurance is iaa1 per SPEC-HIRE -- self-asserted, key custody assumed. Presence: decide deliberately. ssh.rs claims NONE and documents why (an agent key with no passphrase and no confirm flag signs without prompting anybody). gpg-agent is different: it often DOES prompt for a passphrase via pinentry, and a key cached in the agent does not. So the same key can prove with or without a human depending on cache state. That makes gpg the first source where proof cost (persona-jl4j.3) is DYNAMIC rather than static, which is worth getting right here rather than discovering later.

Do not claim presence from the mere fact that pinentry could have appeared.
acceptance_criteria: A signature over the daemon's challenge, verified against the candidate's key; presence claimed only when a human actually authenticated; proof cost reported honestly given agent cache state.
